title: Token stream coalescer and unicode-merge optimizer for prefill hot path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce CPU prefill overhead for mid-to-large prompts (64-2k tokens) by merging adjacent unicode/whitespace runs into coalesced subtokens and introducing a hardware-aware alignment pass so downstream SIMD kernels and kernel-selection heuristics see fewer fragments. This ticket covers the runtime-side prefill optimizer (in the ingest path) plus a small compatibility shim so existing decode schedulers and KV-cache semantics are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end p95 prefill CPU time reduced by >= 20% on representative 256-token prompt mix compared to baseline.
2) No change to tokenization correctness (round-trip tests + fuzz coverage).
3) Integration tests pass for streaming and non-streaming prefill flows.
4) Kernel selection metrics (chosen kernel per-model) show increased use of vectorized normalize kernel for short-run inputs without increasing endpoint latency SLO misses.
implementation_notes: Design a two-stage prefill optimizer: (A) run-length merge pass that collapses consecutive unicode runs and whitespace sequences into single coalesced fragments; (B) alignment hint pass that emits byte-alignment markers for SIMD-friendly chunk sizes (32/64 bytes) so kernel-selection can prefer vectorized normalizer kernels.
Keep tokenizer deterministic: emit mapping table from coalesced fragments back to original offsets for KV cache index and token->string reconstruction.

Introduce a tiny LRU cache keyed by normalized fragment fingerprint (content + model tokenizer id) for hot prefixes. Cache entries store coalesced fragment -> sequence of subtokens. Eviction tuned to avoid memory pressure on high-concurrency hosts.
Expose a runtime flag `--coalescer-mode={off,hybrid,aggressive}` gated behind a feature flag and controlled by rollout policy in console so we can A/B test with dedicated and hosted customers.

Ensure kernel-selection pipeline receives alignment hints; extend kernel profile metadata to include expected input fragment sizes so scheduler can make placement decisions (CPU vs. HW-accelerated path).
benchmarks_and_findings: Microbenchmarks (local c6a-like instance): baseline median CPU prefill 18.3ms for 256-token prompts. After coalescer+alignment: median 13.8ms (24.6% improvement).
p95 improved from 42.1ms -> 30.2ms in mixed-language prompt set (English + Japanese + emojis).
Memory overhead: LRU cache steady-state ~1.7MB per worker for workload with 10k unique fragments; can be tuned by cache size flag.

Edge case: extremely heterogeneous short-chunk inputs (many 1-2 byte tokens) do not benefit; in aggressive mode we saw some regression for <8-token prompts. Hybrid default avoids regressions by skipping coalescing when input length < 16 tokens.
Kernel routing: vectorized normalizer kernel usage increased 32% for flows with coalescer hints, reducing scalar kernel scheduling pressure and improving decode throughput under high concurrency.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect offset mapping could break KV cache hits. Mitigation: comprehensive round-trip tests, property-based tests, and cross-checks with existing session replay logs.
Risk: Cache poisoning / collision. Mitigation: use 128-bit fingerprint (XXH3 + model id) and validate content on hit, fall back to re-tokenize on mismatch.
Risk: CPU regressions for tiny prompts when aggressive mode is enabled. Mitigation: hybrid default policy with short-input bypass and rollout canary to 10% of traffic.
plan_and_timeline: Week 1 (design + proto): implement coalescer pass and alignment hint in prefill path, unit tests.
Week 2 (integration): add LRU fragment cache, kernel-selection hint plumbing, end-to-end tests.
Week 3 (canary + metrics): enable hybrid mode on internal staging, run workload generator to collect p50/p95 and kernel routing metrics.
Week 4 (rollout): incremental rollout to hosted traffic with fallback policy; monitor cost and SLO dashboards.
